Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Evan Ruiz (Redwood SE), Priya Sethi (Auric Head of Platform), Liam O'Connor (Auric Security Eng), Jessica Vance (Auric PM)
summary: Quick product walkthrough focused on data handling controls: request storage toggles, logging redaction, PII scrubbing, and Optimize recommendations for reducing token costs. Customer is evaluating hosted vs private deployment for a B2B analytics assistant; main concerns: retention policy enforcement, KMS integration, and audit logs. Agreed pilot scope and next steps to run benchmarks and exchange security docs.
topics: API flags for storing request metadata vs full payload
Optimize: batching, KV cache, quantization suggestions
Private deployment considerations: VPC, KMS, audit logs
transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time today. Quick intro, I'm Maya, AE on the platform team, and Evan's our SE.
[00:08] Priya (Auric): Hi, thanks. We have about 45 minutes, hope that's OK.
[00:12] Evan (Redwood SE): Yep perfect. We'll jump straight into the console demo — show storage toggles, redaction rules, and then the API flags.
[00:18] Liam (Auric): Brief note — security's top of mind, we need KMS integration details and how retention is enforced, plus proof of deletion for ejected data.
[00:27] Maya: Absolutely. We'll cover KMS, audit trails, and the lifecycle. Quick agenda slide — console first, then API flags and Optimize recommendations, and end with pilot scope. (shared: https://drive.redwood/demo/auric-data-controls)
[00:40] Jessica: Sounds good. Around deployment, we're still deciding between hosted with strict retention toggles and a private VPC. Latency targets are 150ms p50 for short queries, so cost is a factor too.
[00:55] Evan: Good to know. On latency vs cost — we typically advise hosted for quickest time to value, and Dedicated/Private when you need capacity isolation or specific KMS/HSM hardware. For retention we have three modes you can flip per-route: Persist, Ephemeral, and Metadata-only.
[01:12] Evan: (clicks) I'm in the Console now — top right is the route configuration. You can set request_storage: persist | ephemeral | metadata_only, plus a retention TTL if persist.
[01:25] Priya: Can we override at the API level? We have downstream services that call the Redwood API directly.
[01:29] Maya: Yes — there are API flags. You can pass x-redwood-storage: ephemeral or set x-redwood-redact-pii: true. Those are honored by the control plane and show up in audit logs.
[01:42] Liam: Audit logs — what's retained in them? We can't keep full requests for more than 30 days.
[01:47] Evan: Audit logs capture metadata: who called, auth identity, route, model version, decision (persist/ephemeral), and a hash of the request payload for traceability. Full payload retention only if route set to persist; otherwise payload is dropped after processing and KV cache traces are truncated. Note: sometimes transcripts show KV cash — sorry that is a transcribe bug.
[02:10] Jessica: And redaction? We need PII removed from logs but still be able to debug model regressions.
[02:16] Evan: We have layered redaction. First pass is automatic PII detection (names, ssn, emails, phone) with configurable rules. Second pass is rule-based scrubbing — you can add regex rules per-route. Third, you can configure 'debug tokens' that allow temporary unredacted capture for a narrow window — only available in private/dedicated with RBAC gating.
[02:40] Priya: That 'debug tokens' feature — we may need that during initial integration. Is it accessible in Hosted?
[02:45] Maya: In hosted it's available but restricted — requires an approval flow and we record the justification in the audit log. For private, you can set local approval workflows.
[02:54] Liam: KMS — we run AWS KMS. How do you integrate key material?
[02:58] Evan: We support envelope encryption with customer-managed keys in AWS KMS or GCP KMS. For private deployments we can also support on-prem HSMs. The console shows you the KMS config and key rotation policy.
[03:10] Priya: Good. For regulatory audits we need proof of deletion — how do you demonstrate that persisted requests were deleted on request?
[03:16] Maya: We emit a deletion event and a signed tombstone in the audit log with a retention id. That becomes part of the audit export and can be verified against storage bucket manifests. We'll share the exact export format in the security pack.
[03:30] Jessica: Could you demo configuring a route to be metadata_only and then show what appears in the logs?
[03:34] Evan: Sure. Changing route now. (click) Route set to metadata_only, simulate a request...
[03:40] System (transcript note): simulated request payload omitted from this recording for privacy.
[03:45] Evan: Audit log entry — timestamp, caller id, route, model, hash, and redaction status. No payload string. I'll also show the console view where it highlights redaction matches and the regex rule applied.
[04:00] Liam: If we need to keep embeddings for analytics but not text, is that configurable?
[04:04] Evan: Yes. Embeddings can be sent to a separate storage sink and have independent retention. You can set embedding_storage: persist | ephemeral and add filters to strip source text.
[04:14] Priya: On the API side, what's the best practice for toggling storage per-request? We're integrating via a proxy.
[04:20] Maya: Best practice: set route-level defaults in the Console and let the proxy set x-redwood-storage for edge cases. Treat per-request toggles as overrides only for exceptional flows to avoid audit complexity.
[04:33] Jessica: We're worried about developers accidentally leaving persist on. Any guardrails?
[04:37] Evan: Yes, there's a policy engine — you can enforce 'no persist' for certain environments (prod/test) and require approval for any persist change. We also surface warnings in the Console and in CI via config-as-code checks.
[04:52] Priya: About redaction accuracy — do you have metrics?
[04:56] Evan: We publish redaction precision/recall estimates per detector, but it's workload dependent. We recommend adding a small sampling pipeline for the first two weeks of a pilot to validate.
[05:07] Maya: (quick share) Also worth mentioning Optimize — it can analyze your workload and recommend batching, max_tokens, and whether a quantized variant of a model will meet latency while saving cost. For PII-heavy prompts Optimize can suggest pre-prompting that moves identifiers to a metadata bag instead of raw text.
[05:25] Liam: Interesting — pre-prompting to move sensitive fields helps, but our front-end can't easily change payload shape. Does the API accept a metadata object separate from user input?
[05:33] Evan: Yes, accepted schema: input_text and metadata map. Metadata is never included in model input unless you explicitly merge it; it's stored separately when route config says so.
[05:43] Jessica: About the pilot — we want to run a 2-week test hitting our QA corpus for retention enforcement and run 1k requests for latency profiling. What's involved?
[05:50] Maya: We'll provision a sandbox route with your KMS key (or a test key), set retention policies, and Evan will run the benchmark. We'll also give limited debug tokens for a week so you can verify redaction.
[06:02] Priya: Can you also show us the audit export format? We need to slot that into our SIEM ingestion.
[06:07] Evan: Yes — JSON lines with fields: timestamp, actor, route, action, decision, payload_hash, redaction_flags, storage_mode. I'll attach an example in the follow-up.
[06:20] (brief crosstalk)
[06:25] Jessica: One more question — data ejection: if a user requests deletion, how long until it's removed and what's the guarantee?
[06:31] Evan: Deletion requests start an async workflow. For persisted data in hosted we guarantee deletion within 72 hours and a signed deletion record. For dedicated/private depends on your infra, but we provide the same signed tombstones. We'll include SLA language in the contract.
[06:47] Liam: Any known limitations? For instance, with extremely long context windows — does redaction happen before model context assembly?
[06:54] Evan: Redaction is inline as part of request processing before we pass tokens to the model. For very long contexts we do streaming redaction and you may see partial redaction markers — add post-processing checks if you need deterministic removal.
[07:10] Priya: About cost — if we keep metadata_only but still do embeddings, does that add notable cost?
[07:16] Evan: Embedding compute is separate — metadata-only reduces token storage cost but embedding compute cost is unchanged. Optimize can help drop embedding frequency or downsample vectors for analytics.
[07:29] Maya: Wrapping up — sounds like pilot with sandbox route + benchmark + security pack is the agreed next step. We'll send SOC2, KMS integration guide, audit export example, and Evan will share the benchmark script.
[07:42] Priya: Good. One ask — can you include estimated cost delta for ephemeral vs persist at our projected 100k/mo requests?
[07:48] Maya: We'll run those numbers and include in the follow-up.
[07:52] Jessica: Thanks everyone.
[07:54] Maya: Thanks — we'll follow up with an email and scheduling invite.
[07:58] (meeting ends)

Notes on transcription: occasional speaker mislabels (system sometimes shows Speaker 4), 'KV cache' got transcribed as 'KV cash' in places, some interrupted phrases and filler words retained to preserve authenticity.
